Nuevo Laredo Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal highlighted the municipal government's technology advances, including free internet in 120 public spaces and about 130,000 citizen reports handled through the SIGA platform, according to Tamaulipas Habla.

Free connectivity is now offered in hospitals, parks and recreational spaces, the report said. The “Conéctate” program is aimed at university students to make internet access easier and keep a lack of mobile data from affecting their academic work.

Canturosas Villarreal said internet access matters because students struggle when they run out of data, noting that the internet is now a fundamental tool for classes, homework and research, according to the report.

The SIGA system has strengthened communication between residents and municipal authorities, the report said, with reports made through the 072 line and digital platforms, each assigned a tracking number so residents can follow up.

On safety, Canturosas Villarreal said Nuevo Laredo ranks among the five cities in Mexico with the best public perception of safety, a result she credited to coordination with Gov. Américo Villarreal Anaya, President Claudia Sheinbaum and law enforcement at all three levels of government, according to Tamaulipas Habla.

She also said Nuevo Laredo maintains zero public debt, after paying off municipal financial commitments early whose original payment term ran to 2033, without suspending public works, scholarship programs, social support or municipal services, the report said.

Sources:

  • Tamaulipas Habla, “Nuevo Laredo fortalece conectividad digital,” Oct. 29, 2026
